e: Fifteen people are killed in an attack by Islamist militants on Madegoua village near Makary, Far North Region.
Cameroon wins the Women's Africa Cup of Nations for the first time, defeating Malawi 3–0 in the final in Rabat, Morocco.
Pope Leo XIV arrives in Cameroon for a three-day visit.

Parliament approves a constitutional amendment to reintroduce the position of vice president, allowing the appointee to automatically succeed President Biya in the event of death, resignation, or incapacity.
Théodore Datouo is elected as president of the National Assembly, replacing Cavaye Yeguié Djibril after 34 years.
The United Kingdom suspends the issuance of student visas to Cameroonian nationals as part of efforts to reduce asylum requests.
A court-martial in Yaounde convicts three soldiers for their role in the killing of 21 civilians in the Ngarbuh massacre in 2020 and sentences them to up to 10 years' imprisonment.

A freelance journalist on assignment for the Associated Press is assaulted by police and briefly detained alongside three other reporters and a lawyer in Yaoundé, while attempting to report on African migrants recently deported from the United States.
Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea sign an agreement to jointly extract natural gas from the Yoyo-Yolanda field.
At least 15 people are killed in an attack by gunmen on the settlement of Gidado in Ndu, Northwest Region.
